words.definition: A device, such as a rhyme or pattern, that helps a person recall information.
words.example: To learn the planets, she used the mnemonic 'My Very Educated Mother Just Served Us Nachos.'
words.mnemonic: From the Greek Mnemosyne, goddess of memory; the silent 'm' is a memory trick in itself.

words.definition: The act of calling the past back to mind, or a patient's recounted medical history.
words.example: During intake, the doctor recorded the patient's anamnesis, tracing every symptom back to its onset.
words.mnemonic: 'ana-' (back, again) + '-mnesis' (memory) — the exact opposite of amnesia, which loses it.

words.definition: A fond memory of a past event, or the act of dwelling on such memories.
words.example: Over coffee, Grandpa drifted into a long reminiscence about summers on the lake.
words.mnemonic: Hear 'RE-MIND-essence' — the essence of re-minding yourself of old times.

words.definition: Serving to bring something similar to mind; suggestive of another person, place, or time.
words.example: The smell of chalk was reminiscent of her very first classroom decades ago.
words.mnemonic: Shares its root with 'remind' — something reminiscent RE-MINDS you of the past.

words.definition: Strongly fragrant, or strongly suggestive of something through smell or association.
words.example: The kitchen was redolent of cinnamon and freshly baked bread.
words.mnemonic: Latin 'olere' means to smell (like 'odor'); 'red-OLE-nt' hides that scent inside it.

words.definition: Bringing strong images, memories, or feelings vividly to mind.
words.example: Her evocative description of the storm made listeners shiver as though soaked.
words.mnemonic: 'e-' (out) + 'voc' (voice/call, as in 'vocal') — it calls feelings out of you.

words.definition: A sentimental, wistful longing for a period or place in the past.
words.example: Scrolling through old photos filled him with nostalgia for his college years.
words.mnemonic: Greek 'nostos' (homecoming) + 'algos' (pain) — literally the ache to return home.

words.definition: A state of being pleasantly lost in one's own thoughts; a daydream.
words.example: Staring out the train window, she slipped into a reverie and missed her stop.
words.mnemonic: From French 'rêver,' to dream; picture your mind REV-ing off into a dream.

words.definition: The state of being completely forgotten, or a condition of total unawareness.
words.example: The once-famous singer faded into oblivion, her records left to gather dust.
words.mnemonic: Same root as 'oblivious' — to be unaware; oblivion is where the forgotten go.

words.definition: To erase or wipe out completely, as a mark or a record.
words.example: The court agreed to expunge the arrest from his record after five clean years.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'ex-SPONGE' — take a sponge and wipe it entirely away.

words.definition: To destroy utterly or wipe out every trace of something.
words.example: The flood obliterated the village, leaving no sign a town had ever stood there.
words.mnemonic: Latin 'littera' (letter) — 'OB-LITER-ate' means to strike out the letters entirely.

words.definition: To destroy something completely by pulling it out at the root.
words.example: Health workers hope to eradicate the disease before the decade ends.
words.mnemonic: Latin 'radix' (root, like 'radish') — 'e-RADIC-ate' pulls it out by the roots.

words.definition: Impossible to destroy, remove, or pull out at the root.
words.example: Despite the reforms, an ineradicable distrust of the government lingered for generations.
words.mnemonic: 'in-' (not) + 'eradicable' (able to be rooted out) — this root simply won't come out.

words.definition: To honor and keep alive the memory of a person or event, often with a ceremony.
words.example: A bronze plaque was installed to commemorate the soldiers who fell there.
words.mnemonic: 'com-' (together) + 'memor' (memory, as in 'memorial') — together we hold it in memory.

words.definition: To honor someone or something so they are not forgotten, often with a lasting tribute.
words.example: The town memorialized the fallen soldiers with a bronze statue in the square.
words.mnemonic: memorial + -ize — to turn something into a memorial that keeps it present.

words.definition: Affecting the mind below the level of conscious awareness.
words.example: The ad used subliminal images flashed too quickly for viewers to consciously notice.
words.mnemonic: sub- (below) + limen (threshold) — beneath the threshold where you notice things.

words.definition: To fade away and vanish, like mist dissolving into air.
words.example: The morning fog began to evanesce as the sun climbed higher over the valley.
words.mnemonic: sounds like 'ever-vanish' — it drifts off like vapor and is gone.

words.definition: Lasting only a very short time before passing away.
words.example: The fugacious beauty of the cherry blossoms lasts barely a week each spring.
words.mnemonic: shares the root fug- (flee) with 'fugitive' — it flees almost as soon as it arrives.

words.definition: The small part left over after most has been removed or used up.
words.example: After the water evaporated, a chalky residuum coated the bottom of the beaker.
words.mnemonic: sounds like 'residue' — the stubborn bit sitting at the bottom.

words.definition: Beautiful or sad in a way that lingers in the mind.
words.example: Her haunting melody stayed with me for days after the concert ended.
words.mnemonic: like a ghost that haunts a house — it refuses to leave your thoughts.

words.definition: The act of looking inward to examine your own thoughts and feelings.
words.example: A week alone in the cabin gave him time for quiet introspection.
words.mnemonic: intro- (inward) + spect (look) — you point the gaze back at yourself.

words.definition: The act of reviewing or thinking about events from the past.
words.example: In retrospection, she realized the warning signs had been there all along.
words.mnemonic: retro- (back) + spect (look) — turning your eyes toward what already happened.

words.definition: Able to hold on to or keep things, especially facts in the mind.
words.example: With his retentive mind, he recalled phone numbers he'd heard only once.
words.mnemonic: from 'retain' (ten- = hold) — a grip that keeps everything it grabs.

words.definition: A physical trace left in the brain where a memory is stored.
words.example: Neuroscientists spent years hunting for the engram behind a single learned fact.
words.mnemonic: en- (in) + -gram (something written) — a note written into the brain's tissue.

words.definition: A person who has lost the ability to recall past events.
words.example: The amnesiac woke in a hospital bed unable to name his own children.
words.mnemonic: a- (without) + -mnesia (memory, from Mnemosyne) — someone left without a past.

words.definition: A blank space or missing part, especially in a text or argument.
words.example: A crucial lacuna in the manuscript left scholars guessing at the story's ending.
words.mnemonic: sounds like 'lagoon' — an empty hollow where something should be.

words.definition: To escape or avoid capture, detection, or understanding.
words.example: The fox managed to elude the hounds by doubling back through the stream.
words.mnemonic: e- (out) + -lude (play) — it slips out and dodges just as you reach.

words.definition: To be a sign or warning of something that will happen.
words.example: Dark clouds massing on the horizon betoken a storm before nightfall.
words.mnemonic: be- + token — to act as a token, a sign pointing to what's coming.

words.definition: A slight suspicion or vague hint about something.
words.example: She had an inkling that her surprise party was being planned behind her back.
words.mnemonic: picture one tiny drop of 'ink' — just a faint trace, barely a mark.

words.definition: A faint, unsteady light, or a small sign of something.
words.example: Through the fog she caught a glimmer of the distant lighthouse beam.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'shimmer' — a tiny, wavering shimmer of light in the dark.

words.definition: A state of dreamy, pleasant tiredness and lack of energy.
words.example: The summer heat wrapped the porch in a heavy languor that left everyone dozing.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'linger' — too relaxed to move, you just linger.

words.definition: A condition of sluggishness, drowsiness, and lack of enthusiasm.
words.example: After the huge meal a deep lethargy settled over him and nothing could rouse him.
words.mnemonic: From Lethe, the mythic river of forgetful sleep — drink it and you go dull and drowsy.

words.definition: A dazed, near-unconscious state in which one can barely think or react.
words.example: He drank until he sank into a stupor and slept upright in his chair.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'stupid' — too dazed to think a single clear thought.

words.definition: The period of feeble, childish mental decline in very old age.
words.example: In his dotage, Grandfather often mistook his grandchildren for his own brothers.
words.mnemonic: 'Dot-age' — the age when a doddering mind goes dotty and forgetful.

words.definition: The condition of no longer being practiced or in active use.
words.example: The old dueling statutes fell into desuetude, and no court ever enforced them again.
words.mnemonic: 'De-' (un) + Latin 'suetus' (accustomed) — un-accustomed, dropped from custom.

words.definition: A state of temporary suspension or pause, awaiting later settlement.
words.example: The building plans were held in abeyance until the funding dispute was resolved.
words.mnemonic: Say 'a-BAY-ance' — the matter is kept at bay, waiting on the sidelines.

words.definition: A gap between two rulers or governments when normal authority is suspended.
words.example: During the interregnum after the king's death, rival dukes fought for the throne.
words.mnemonic: 'Inter' (between) + 'regnum' (reign) — the empty space between reigns.

words.definition: To bring back to life or restore fresh energy to something.
words.example: Cold water and strong coffee revivified the exhausted climbers before the final push.
words.mnemonic: 'Re' (again) + 'vivi' (life, as in vivid, vivacious) — make lively again.

words.definition: A period when illness eases or disappears, or the pardon of a debt.
words.example: After a grueling year of chemotherapy, her cancer finally went into remission.
words.mnemonic: 'Re-mission' — the disease is sent away on a mission (Latin 'remittere', to send back).

words.definition: A person or spirit that returns, especially one come back from the dead.
words.example: Villagers swore the pale figure by the graveyard was a revenant of the drowned sailor.
words.mnemonic: From French 'revenir' (to return) — the one who comes back.

words.definition: To chat casually, or to invent false memories while believing them true.
words.example: The amnesiac patient would confabulate vivid stories about a voyage he had never taken.
words.mnemonic: 'Con' + 'fable' + 'ate' — you eat up fables, cooking up tales as fact.

words.definition: To think or talk fondly about pleasant experiences from the past.
words.example: The old friends spent the whole evening reminiscing about their college days.
words.mnemonic: 'Re-mini-scene' — replaying little scenes from the past in your head.

words.definition: To destroy or remove something completely, as if pulling out its roots.
words.example: The campaign set out to extirpate the invasive weed from every field in the valley.
words.mnemonic: 'Ex' (out) + Latin 'stirps' (root) — tear it out by the roots; think 'exterminate'.

words.definition: To cut out or remove a part, especially surgically or from a piece of writing.
words.example: The editor told her to excise the entire third paragraph, which added nothing.
words.mnemonic: ex- (out) + Latin caedere (to cut) — think 'ex-scissors': scissors cut something out.

words.definition: To leave out or slur over something, especially a sound or syllable in speech.
words.example: In fast talk we elide the middle of 'camera,' saying 'cam-ra.'
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'a slide' — words slide together and letters slip away.

words.definition: To make someone accustomed to something difficult or unpleasant through repeated exposure.
words.example: Years on the trauma ward had inured the nurse to the sight of blood.
words.mnemonic: Read it as 'in-your' — hardship gets in your skin until it stops bothering you.

words.definition: To spread gradually through or over something, filling it with color, light, or feeling.
words.example: A warm glow suffused the room as the sunset poured through the curtains.
words.mnemonic: 'sun-fuse': sunlight fuses across and floods a whole surface.

words.definition: To fill or inspire someone deeply with a feeling, quality, or value.
words.example: Her mentor imbued her with a lifelong respect for careful, honest work.
words.mnemonic: 'im-brew' — you brew feelings into someone until they're steeped in them.

words.definition: To catch sight of or make out something distant or hard to see.
words.example: From the crow's nest the sailor could just descry land on the horizon.
words.mnemonic: 'de-spy' — you spy out something far away, like a seer who scries.

words.definition: To redirect unacceptable urges into socially productive or creative activity.
words.example: He sublimated his anger into marathon training, running until the rage burned off.
words.mnemonic: 'sublime' + ate — you elevate a base urge into something sublime.

words.definition: To fix an idea or habit firmly in someone's mind through persistent instruction.
words.example: The drill sergeant inculcated discipline in the recruits with endless repetition.
words.mnemonic: Latin calx (heel): 'in-CALC-ate' — you stamp it in with your boot heel.

words.definition: To dig up a buried body, or to bring something long hidden back to light.
words.example: Investigators moved to exhume the body to test for poison decades after burial.
words.mnemonic: ex- (out) + Latin humus (ground) — 'ex-humus,' taken out of the earth.

words.definition: Relating to unusually vivid and detailed mental images, like a photographic memory.
words.example: With her eidetic recall, she could quote any page after a single reading.
words.mnemonic: 'I.D.-etic' — the mind IDs and photographs every detail (Greek eidos, image).

words.definition: Expressing sorrow or mournful longing, especially for something lost or past.
words.example: The film's elegiac tone lingered over a vanished world no one could reclaim.
words.mnemonic: From 'elegy,' a mourning poem — elegiac is that poem's grieving mood.

words.definition: A monument honoring people whose remains lie elsewhere or were never recovered.
words.example: The town's cenotaph lists the war dead, though none of them rest there.
words.mnemonic: Greek kenos (empty) + taphos (tomb) — literally an 'empty tomb.'

words.definition: An inscription on a gravestone in memory of the person laid to rest there.
words.example: His epitaph read simply, 'He made people laugh.'
words.mnemonic: epi- (upon) + taphos (tomb) — the words written upon the tomb.

words.definition: A sorrowful poem or song written to mourn someone who has died.
words.example: At the graveside, the poet read an elegy that left the whole family in tears.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like a sad 'eulogy' — an elegy is basically a eulogy set to verse.

words.definition: The lighter, partial shadow at the outer edge of a full shadow.
words.example: During the eclipse we stood in the penumbra, where only part of the sun was hidden.
words.mnemonic: Latin 'paene' (almost) + 'umbra' (shadow) — almost-a-shadow.

words.definition: A jumbled, confused mixture of many unrelated things.
words.example: His excuse was a farrago of half-truths, bad jokes, and irrelevant statistics.
words.mnemonic: From Latin 'far' (grain) — mixed cattle fodder; picture grain, straw, and scraps tossed together.

words.definition: A tiny gap or narrow space between two adjoining things.
words.example: Moss crept into every interstice between the old paving stones.
words.mnemonic: 'Inter' (between) + 'stice' (to stand) — a small space standing between things.

words.definition: A varied collection of assorted items or writings gathered together.
words.example: The junk drawer held a miscellany of buttons, coins, and long-forgotten keys.
words.mnemonic: Cousin of 'miscellaneous' — a miscellany is a heap of the miscellaneous.

words.definition: A container that holds sacred objects or the bodily remains of a saint.
words.example: The cathedral displayed a jeweled reliquary said to enshrine a saint's finger bone.
words.mnemonic: 'Relic' + '-ary' (a place for) — the place where relics are kept.

words.definition: A mixture of many varied and dissimilar elements.
words.example: The stew was a rich melange of vegetables, spices, and yesterday's roast.
words.mnemonic: French 'mélanger' (to mix); hear 'melon-change' — every kind of melon blended in one bowl.

words.definition: To break out or flare up again after a period of calm or dormancy.
words.example: Old grievances began to recrudesce the moment the fragile truce collapsed.
words.mnemonic: 'Re-' (again) + Latin 'crudus' (raw) — a raw wound reopening.

words.definition: The mind's grasp of something new in terms of what it already knows.
words.example: Through apperception, the child fitted the strange new word into ideas she had long understood.
words.mnemonic: 'Apper-' like 'appear' + '-ception' — new things appear and fold into what you grasp.

words.definition: To shed or cast off an outer layer, such as dead skin.
words.example: As it grows, the snake will slough its worn skin and slither out anew.
words.mnemonic: Say it 'sluff' — to sluff off the old, dead layer.

words.definition: Extremely old-fashioned or belonging to a very ancient time.
words.example: His antediluvian attitude toward computers made a smartphone seem like sorcery to him.
words.mnemonic: 'Ante-' (before) + 'diluvian' (the deluge) — from before Noah's Flood.

words.definition: To shut someone in or imprison them behind walls.
words.example: The hermit chose to immure himself in a tiny stone cell for a year of silence.
words.mnemonic: 'Im-' (in) + Latin 'murus' (wall) — to seal someone inside walls.

words.definition: A partial or total loss of the ability to recall past events.
words.example: After the car crash, she suffered amnesia and could not recognize her own children.
words.mnemonic: a- (without) + -mnesia (memory, as in 'mnemonic') = without memory.

words.definition: An object kept as a reminder of a person, place, or event.
words.example: She kept the little seashell as a memento of their honeymoon by the ocean.
words.mnemonic: Sounds like 'memory' + 'note' — a note that jogs your memory.

words.definition: The act of keeping something in mind or honoring the memory of it.
words.example: The town held a moment of remembrance for the soldiers who never returned.
words.mnemonic: re- (again) + 'member' — to bring a 'member' of the past back into mind.

words.definition: To bring back to mind something from the past.
words.example: Try as he might, he could not recollect where he had left his keys.
words.mnemonic: re- + 'collect' — to gather your scattered memories together again.

words.definition: The ability to keep or hold onto something, such as facts or fluid.
words.example: Repeating the list aloud each night improved her retention of the new vocabulary.
words.mnemonic: Latin 'tenere' means to hold — same root as 'tenant,' who holds property.

words.definition: A drug or drink that banishes grief and brings blissful forgetting.
words.example: He drank deeply, hoping the wine would be a nepenthe for his heartbreak.
words.mnemonic: ne- (not) + Greek 'penthos' (grief) = 'no grief.'

words.definition: To find and bring back something that was lost or stored away.
words.example: The dog splashed into the lake to retrieve the stick her owner had thrown.
words.mnemonic: Picture a golden 'retriever' — a dog bred to bring things back.

words.definition: Not paying attention to or caring about something important.
words.example: Unmindful of the time, she read until the library lights suddenly went dark.
words.mnemonic: un- (not) + 'mindful' — literally 'not minding' what surrounds you.

words.definition: Careless and paying no attention to danger or advice.
words.example: Heedless of the warning signs, the swimmers waded past the roped-off area.
words.mnemonic: 'Heed' means to pay attention; '-less' strips it away — no heed given.

words.definition: Feeling a wistful, sentimental longing for happier times in the past.
words.example: Old photographs made her nostalgic for summers spent at her grandmother's farm.
words.mnemonic: Greek 'nostos' (homecoming) + 'algos' (pain) — the ache to return home.

words.definition: A small item held onto because of the memories attached to it.
words.example: Her grandmother's thimble is a keepsake she will never sell or throw away.
words.mnemonic: 'Keep' + 'sake' — something you keep for the sake of remembering.

words.definition: Lasting for an extremely long time; permanent and hard to destroy.
words.example: The Roman aqueducts proved perdurable, still standing after nearly two thousand years.
words.mnemonic: per- (through) + Latin 'durare' (to last) — lasting all the way through.
